sit_010:n1.prompt:
You are helping me understand a Delaware franchise tax delinquency notice for my company so I can decide how and when to cure it. This step is about reading and summarizing only. Do not file or pay anything.

Ask me for anything missing:
- my company's exact legal name and Delaware file number
- the notice text or a scan/PDF of it
- my authorized share count and the total gross assets from my last tax return, if I have them

Actions:
1. Read the notice. Pull out what was missed (the annual report and franchise tax due March 1), the tax year, any amounts stated, and the current standing status.
2. Open the State of Delaware Division of Corporations franchise tax page at https://corp.delaware.gov/frtax/. Check the current rules there: the March 1 due date, the $200 late-filing penalty, interest at 1.5% per month on unpaid tax, and the loss of good standing (8 Del. C. §§ 502, 504). Treat the state's own pages as authoritative. If anything on the state's pages differs from what I've written here, flag the difference.
3. Estimate what I owe today: tax due, plus the $200 penalty, plus 1.5% monthly interest for each month since March 1. Show your math. Also show how the total grows if I wait one, two, or three more months.
4. Note whether the billed tax looks like it was computed with the authorized-shares method. If it does, tell me that a recomputation using the assumed-par-value method may lower it significantly. That recomputation is the next step, so just flag it here.
5. Explain in plain terms what "not in good standing" blocks, such as fundraising diligence and good-standing certificates.

Done looks like a one-page summary with these parts:
- what was missed
- a cost table (now versus waiting)
- standing consequences
- discrepancies with the state's site
- a recommended next step

Then stop for human sign-off. The decision to cure now, and any filing or payment, is mine. Do not log into the state's filing system, submit a report, or make a payment on my behalf.

sit_010:n2.prompt:
You are helping me cure a missed Delaware franchise tax and annual report filing for my corporation. For this step, recompute the franchise tax using the Assumed Par Value Capital method before I react to the large bill the default Authorized Shares method often produces. Do not file or pay anything yet; this step is calculation only.

Ask me for anything missing:
- The corporation's exact legal name and Delaware file number
- The tax year(s) that are delinquent
- Total authorized shares, broken out by class, with the par value of each class (from the certificate of incorporation)
- Total issued and outstanding shares as of the end of each delinquent tax year
- Total gross assets as of fiscal year end, as reported on the federal return's balance sheet (Form 1120, Schedule L), or my best figure if no return has been filed yet

Actions:
1. Open the Delaware Division of Corporations franchise tax calculator at https://corp.delaware.gov/frtaxcalc/ and read its instructions.
2. Run the Authorized Shares method so I can see the baseline figure.
3. Run the Assumed Par Value Capital method with my issued shares, gross assets, and authorized shares and par values. Repeat for each delinquent year.
4. Note the lower result for each year. The state lets you pay the lower amount, but the annual report must include the issued shares and gross assets figures that support the alternative method.
5. From the Division's own pages, note the late-filing penalty and monthly interest that apply to the delinquency. Do not rely on remembered figures. Record the source URL for each number.

Done looks like a short report for each delinquent year with:
- The tax under each method
- The method to use and the exact inputs entered
- The applicable penalty and interest, with the pages they came from
- An estimated total amount to cure
- Any input you assumed or could not verify

Flag clearly if the inputs look inconsistent, for example issued shares greater than authorized shares or gross assets left blank.

sit_010:n3.prompt:
You are helping me cure my Delaware corporation's franchise tax delinquency. I missed the March 1 annual report and franchise tax, so the company is likely 'not in good standing.' This step is to file the overdue annual report and pay online through the Delaware Division of Corporations at https://corp.delaware.gov/paytaxes/. Filing and payment happen only in the state's own portal. There is no public filing API, and the entry page has an image CAPTCHA, so you prepare everything and I complete the gate, the filing and the payment.

Ask me for anything missing:
- exact legal entity name and Delaware file number
- the franchise tax figure we recomputed with the assumed-par-value method, plus its inputs (authorized shares, issued shares, gross assets, par value)
- current officer and director names and addresses, the principal place of business, and the number of directors
- the tax year(s) overdue

Then:
1. Read the Division of Corporations pay-taxes and annual-report pages. Confirm the current deadline, the $200 late penalty, and the 1.5% monthly interest stated there (8 Del. C. §§ 502, 504). Flag any figure that differs from what I gave you.
2. Estimate the total due: tax plus penalty plus accrued interest. Show the math and mark it as an estimate. The portal's figure controls.
3. Build a field-by-field checklist of everything the annual report form will ask for, pre-filled with my values. Note any field I still need to supply.
4. If you can open the portal, go as far as the CAPTCHA and stop. Passing the CAPTCHA remains a human step.

Never submit the report, approve payment, or enter payment details on my behalf. Once the checklist and estimate are ready, stop for human sign-off.

Done looks like:
- a verified fee and penalty summary with links to the state pages you used
- the pre-filled form checklist
- the estimated amount due
- a short list of open questions

Report back in that order. After I file and pay, remind me to save the filing confirmation and receipt for the next step, which is confirming good standing is restored.

sit_010:n4.prompt:
You are helping me confirm that my Delaware corporation is back in good standing. I filed an overdue annual franchise tax report and paid the tax, penalty, and interest (8 Del. C. §§ 502, 504). This step verifies the cure on the state's own public entity search.

Inputs (ask me if any are missing):
- My company's exact legal name.
- Its Delaware file number (shown on the annual report or payment receipt).
- The date I paid and my payment confirmation number.

Actions:
1. Open the Delaware Division of Corporations entity status search at https://icis.corp.delaware.gov/ecorp2/services/t/getcompanystatus.
2. Search by file number if you have it, otherwise by exact entity name. If the form shows a verification challenge you cannot complete, pause and ask me to clear it.
3. Read back what the result page shows, including entity name, file number, entity type, and status. If the page says more detail requires a fee, do not pay anything.
4. Interpret the result:
   - If the status indicates good standing, the cure is confirmed.
   - If it still shows a delinquent or other not-in-good-standing status, compare it against my payment date. State processing can lag after an online payment. Tell me whether to recheck later or contact the Division of Corporations directly.
5. Do not order a certificate of good standing, submit any payment, or change any filing. This is a read-only lookup.

Done looks like: the current status, read directly from the state's page, with a clear verdict.

Report back with:
- The result fields exactly as displayed.
- A screenshot or saved copy of the result page, if your tools allow.
- The date and time of the lookup.
- Your conclusion: restored, not yet updated, or problem.
- A recommended next action, such as requesting a good-standing certificate for investor diligence, rechecking on a specific date, or calling the Division.

Finally, remind me to set a recurring calendar reminder well ahead of the March 1 annual report and franchise tax deadline, so this doesn't happen again.

sit_010:n5.prompt:
You are helping me fix the root cause of my Delaware corporation's missed franchise tax filing so it doesn't happen again. The annual report and franchise tax are due March 1 each year (8 Del. C. §§ 502, 504). Missing it brings a $200 penalty, 1.5% monthly interest, and loss of good standing. Verify the current deadline and amounts on the Delaware Division of Corporations' own website before relying on them.

Ask me for anything missing: my company's legal name and Delaware file number, my registered agent's name and the contact email/phone they have on file, which calendar I use, and who besides me should get reminders (co-founder, finance lead, accountant).

Please:
1. Confirm the March 1 deadline on the Delaware Division of Corporations site and note the link.
2. Create a recurring annual calendar event for March 1 in my calendar, using your configured credentials. Add reminders around 60, 30, 14, and 3 days before. In the description, include the state filing page link, my file number, and a note to compute the tax with the assumed-par-value method before paying.
3. Invite the backup people I name so the reminder doesn't depend on one inbox.
4. Check whether my registered agent's account lists the right contact email for compliance notices. If you can view it with my configured access, report what's on file. If you can't, draft a short email asking them to confirm or update the contact and send reminders to both me and the backup.
5. Suggest a filter or label so notices from the agent and the state skip spam and promotions folders.

Done means the recurring event exists with reminders and invitees, and the registered agent contact is confirmed or a request is drafted. Report back with the event details, who was invited, the agent contact status, any draft emails for my review, and anything you couldn't verify.
